chunks: And whatever is in it from Umar ibn Qays Al-Maṣir, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan - may Allah have mercy on them - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah Al-Barqi, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and others, from Umar ibn Qays Al-Maṣir.

key_terms.أَبِي: My father (referring to Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Al-Husayn, known as Al-Shaykh Al-Saduq's father)
key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الْبَ: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah Al-Barqi, a well-known hadith scholar
key_terms.سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Sa'd ibn Abdullah, a major narrator of hadith
key_terms.عُمَرَ بْنِ قَيْسٍ الْمَاصِرِ: Umar ibn Qays Al-Maṣir, a prominent companion and narrator of hadith
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ الْحَسَنِ: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a key scholar in the transmission chain

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Umar ibn Qays Al-Maṣir verified in Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih?
ai.summary: This passage functions as a critical colophon in *Man La Yahduruhu Al-Faqih*, verifying the authenticity of Umar ibn Qays Al-Maṣir’s narrations by tracing them through Al-Saduq’s personal teachers, including his father and Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan. It underscores the scholarly rigor of the Kufan tradition, emphasizing the direct link between the compiler and the early Imami authorities to validate the legal and theological content of the hadith.
